You asked: Add a whisper(text) function in src/whisper.js that returns the text in lower case with three dots at the end. Export it from src/index.js with tests.
App name: word-tools: whisper
Summary: word-tools is a small library of text helpers that programmers can use in their own code. This change adds a new helper called whisper. It takes a piece of text, makes the first letter a capital and everything else lower case, and adds "..." on the end, so "hELLO WORLD"
Summary: becomes "Hello world...".

Marked as routine work for “Add whisper(text) and export it from the package entry point”: the team tries its lightest AI first and moves up if the checks fail.
Choice made for you: whisper follows the same pattern as capitalize: an ES module named export in its own file, src/whisper.js, re-exported from src/index.js, with a one-line doc comment.
Choice made for you: Following the owner's change: only the very first character of the whole text is upper-cased. Everything after it is lower-cased, including the first letters of later words. "Hello World" becomes "Hello world...".
Choice made for you: The capitalising rule is the same as the existing capitalize helper: upper-case text[0] and lower-case the rest. If the text starts with a space or punctuation, that character is left as is, so whisper(" hi") returns " hi...". It does not skip ahead to the
Choice made for you: first letter.
Choice made for you: Non-string input throws a TypeError with the message "whisper expects a string". whisper checks this itself, so the message names whisper and not capitalize.
Choice made for you: An empty string returns "...".
Choice made for you: Three dots are always added, even if the text already ends with dots or other punctuation. whisper("Wait...") returns "Wait......".
Choice made for you: The dots are three ASCII period characters ("..."), not the single ellipsis character (…).
Choice made for you: Case changes use JavaScript's standard toUpperCase()/toLowerCase(), with no locale-specific rules.
Choice made for you: The README gets a short whisper(text) section next to the capitalize one, so the new helper is documented.
Choice made for you: Tests use the built-in node:test and node:assert/strict, like the existing tests, so no dependencies are added.
Name the tests and the code must agree on: This is a library, so it has no UI, routes or HTTP endpoints. The contract is the module API.
